donors.purpose: Go-native persistent SQLite queue and background-job patterns
donors.decision_note: Passive scan clean, but current donor requires Go 1.25 while ECO main declares Go 1.23. Do not force a toolchain upgrade solely for this donor.

donors.purpose: Go 1.23-compatible persistent SQLite job queue with retries, delayed jobs, deduplication, visibility timeouts and cancellable workers
donors.decision_note: Architectural fit is strong, but passive intake found known golang.org/x/mod and golang.org/x/sys dependency vulnerabilities. The fixed x/mod version requires Go 1.25, so do not import this dependency into ECO Go 1.23. Study/adapt the small MIT design only through a separate target-project review.

donors.purpose: Go-native CPU, RAM, disk, process and network measurements including Windows
donors.decision_note: Passive intake found GO-2026-5024 / CVE-2026-39824 in direct golang.org/x/sys v0.41.0 dependency; fixed version is v0.44.0. Requalify a safe upstream revision before integration.

donors.purpose: Lightweight terminal progress display for support and engineering tools
donors.decision_note: Passive scan clean, but current module declares Go 1.25 and this is terminal UI rather than ECO core GUI. Do not add to ECO core merely for progress reporting.

donors.purpose: Primary local inference engine and OpenAI-compatible server foundation
donors.decision_note: Passive intake verified the MIT source and no real leaked credentials. Whole-repository scans found known vulnerabilities in optional Python tooling plus Docker-policy findings, so do not treat the entire repository as a clean dependency set. Qualify only the native Windows x64 CPU/server build and tests first, then evaluate GPU backends separately.

donors.purpose: Windows llama.cpp runtime, GGUF model, launch-profile, multi-server supervision, metrics and local automation patterns
donors.decision_note: Strong architecture fit. Passive intake found no secret findings, no Trivy vulnerability/misconfiguration findings and no Grype vulnerability matches in the scanned source tree. Proceed to isolated upstream-style Windows build/test qualification without publishing an executable.

donors.purpose: Immutable evidence copies, SHA-256 provenance, hash-chained custody, deterministic evidence citations and verified case export patterns
donors.decision_note: Passive runtime-source review is favourable; secret findings were deliberate synthetic fixtures and the detected vulnerable packages were repository CI actions rather than the evidence runtime. Adapt patterns rather than copy wholesale: ECO needs stricter audit-write failure handling, stronger concurrent ID allocation and stronger immutability controls. Qualify upstream tests separately before target-project adaptation.

donors.purpose: Mature Windows service wrapper and process-supervision patterns
donors.decision_note: Prefer using WinSW as a separate upstream service wrapper rather than copying its implementation. Passive findings were concentrated in repository-maintenance GitHub action dependencies, not the service-wrapper code. Qualify the intended upstream build/release path before operational use.
